mainTopic: Whether a שליח can be appointed for what the sender cannot do now; vows to pay for half a נזיר; and נזירות that depends on the birth of a son or child.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבא, who ruled that a שליח for קידושין cannot marry the sender to a woman who was married when the שליח was appointed. The challenge compares this to a promise to pay for a future נזיר's shaving. The גמרא answers that a person only appoints a שליח for something he could do himself right now. It then tests that rule with a ברייתא about a husband who tells his אפוטרופוס to cancel his wife's future vows. Since the חכמים hold that a husband cannot cancel vows in advance, it seems a שליח can do more than the sender. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר, who says a husband can cancel in advance. In that case, the husband appoints a steward only in case he forgets, gets angry or is busy. Next, a משנה discusses two people who each vow to pay for 'shaving half a נזיר', and רבא explains exactly which wording רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a vow to be a נזיר 'when I have a son' depends on a definite son, while 'when I have a child' is fulfilled by any baby.

steps.title: Finishing the comparison to shaving a future נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case of 'I will shave a נזיר' as meaning 'if I find someone who becomes a נזיר.' It applies the same reading to the שליח: 'if you find she got divorced, marry her to me.' This challenges רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means: if I find someone who becomes a נזיר, I will pay for his shaving. Here too, the sender means: if you find that she has become divorced, marry her to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge to רבא by showing how a promise can apply to someone who does not fit the role yet. It says the same could be true of the שליח and a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can commit to bringing a נזיר's offerings even if no one is a נזיר right now, because he means 'whoever becomes one.' In the same way, the sender might mean 'even a woman who is married now, if she later becomes divorced.' If that is right, the sender would be forbidden to her sister, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow of נזירות
I will shave him (I will pay for his shaving offerings)
Marry her to me (do קידושין for me)

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
If I find someone who becomes a nazirite, I will shave him.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier case of a person who says 'I take upon myself to shave a נזיר', meaning he will pay for the offerings.

phrases.english: Here too, this is what he is saying to him:
If you find that she has been divorced, betroth her to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge to רבא that started on the previous page.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a שליח cannot marry the sender to a woman who was married at the time of the appointment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Just as a promise to shave a נזיר covers a future נזיר, appointing a שליח could cover a woman who becomes divorced later.

steps.title: An agent is only for what you could do now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases are different. A person only appoints a שליח for something he himself could do right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: A person appoints a שליח only for something he could do himself right now. For something he cannot do right now, he does not appoint a שליח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by giving a rule about how שליחות works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sender could not marry a married woman at the moment he appointed the שליח, so she is not included in the appointment. Shaving a נזיר is a different matter because it is not about making someone your שליח. This means רבא's ruling stands, and the sender may marry the divorced woman's sister.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that a שליח can only act where the sender could act now, gets tested in the next steps.

phrases.english: They say: A person does not appoint an agent
except for a matter that he can do now;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא מָצֵי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ הַשְׁתָּא
phrases.english: for a matter that he cannot do now,
he does not appoint.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases based on a principle of שליחות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Appointing a שליח might cover a woman who becomes available later, like shaving a future נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שליח is only appointed for what the sender could do at that moment, so a married woman is not included.

steps.title: Challenge from a steward told to cancel future vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the new principle and brings a ברייתא. A husband tells his אפוטרופוס to cancel any vows his wife makes while he is away. רבי יאשיה says the steward cannot cancel them because of a פסוק, and רבי יונתן says he can, because a שליח is like the sender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can't he? Come and hear: If a man tells his אפוטרופוס, 'Cancel all vows my wife makes from now until I come back from a certain place,' and the steward cancels them, you might think they are cancelled. So the פסוק says, 'Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it.' These are the words of רבי יאשיה. רבי יונתן says: everywhere we find that a person's שליח is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge to the rule from step 2 by quoting a ברייתא. Here it only quotes the source; the next step explains why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time he appoints the steward, the husband seemingly cannot cancel vows his wife has not made yet (step 5 shows the חכמים hold this). Yet he still appoints a שליח to cancel them later. רבי יונתן allows it outright, and the next step shows that רבי יאשיה forbids it only because of a special פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Steward, manager of a person's affairs
A person's agent is like himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge only works for רבי יונתן. The next step shows that even רבי יאשיה agrees the steward could cancel the vows if not for the פסוק.

phrases.english: And does he not? Come and hear:
One who says to his steward:
'All vows that my wife will vow
from now until I come back from such-and-such a place
nullify for her,' and he nullified for her,
one might think they would be nullified;
therefore the verse says:
'Her husband may uphold it and her husband may nullify it,'
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.
And Rabbi Yonatan says:

phrases.aramaic: מָצִינוּ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: We have found everywhere that a person's agent is like himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person only appoints a שליח for what he can do now.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A husband appoints a steward to cancel vows that do not exist yet, which he cannot cancel himself right now.

steps.title: Even רבי יאשיה agrees, except for the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יאשיה rules against the steward only because of the פסוק. Without it, the steward could cancel future vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason is that the Torah said 'Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it.' Without that, the אפוטרופוס would be able to cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי יאשיה's reasoning to make the challenge work for both opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יאשיה needs a פסוק to block the steward, the basic rules of שליחות would have let the steward cancel future vows. This means both opinions agree that a שליח can, in principle, be appointed for something that cannot be done yet.

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One said
'Her husband may uphold it and her husband may nullify it,'
but if it were not so,
the steward would be able to nullify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא from step 3 is a problem even for רבי יאשיה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי יאשיה agrees that, without a פסוק, a steward could cancel vows that do not exist yet.

steps.title: The husband himself cannot cancel vows in advance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source showing that a husband cannot uphold or cancel his wife's vows before she makes them, according to חכמים. So the steward could do something the husband cannot do now.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about the husband himself it is taught: If a man tells his wife, 'All vows you make from now until I come back from a certain place shall be upheld,' he has said nothing. If he says 'They are cancelled,' רבי אליעזר says they are cancelled and חכמים say they are not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge by showing that the husband himself cannot cancel future vows. This makes the steward case a clear problem for the rule from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חכמים, a husband's cancellation of vows that have not been made yet does not work. Yet the ברייתא assumed that a steward could cancel future vows if not for the פסוק. So a שליח seems to be able to do what the sender cannot do right now, which goes against step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: He has said nothing (his words have no effect)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge is: a husband cannot cancel future vows himself (says חכמים), yet a steward could have done so if not for the פסוק. That seems to break the rule that a שליח is only for what the sender can do now.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished yet. Step 6 puts the two sources together, and steps 7-9 answer it.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding himself it is taught:
One who says to his wife:
'All vows that you will vow
from now until I come back from such-and-such a place
shall be upheld' — he has said nothing.
'They are hereby nullified' —
phrases.notes: The משנה leaves out the words of the setup, but he means the same 'from now until I come back' case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is nullified,
and the Rabbis say: it is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the second half of the challenge: the husband himself cannot do what the steward could.
steps.raayaObject: That a שליח can be appointed for something the sender cannot do right now.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדרים: according to חכמים, a husband's advance cancellation of future vows is not effective.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge: the steward could act even though the husband can't
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רבא. It assumes רבי יאשיה follows the רבנן, who say a husband cannot cancel vows before they are made. Even so, without the פסוק the steward could cancel them, so a שליח can do something the sender cannot do right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are thinking that when רבי יאשיה spoke, he followed the רבנן, who say the husband cannot cancel vows ahead of time. And still, if the Torah had not said 'her husband upholds it and her husband cancels it,' the steward would have been able to cancel them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts together steps 4 and 5 and finishes its question on רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that only the פסוק stops the steward. Step 5 showed that, according to the רבנן, the husband himself cannot cancel future vows. Putting these together, a שליח could do something the sender cannot do now. That goes against the rule from step 2, which was used to defend רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters our mind / we are now assuming
According to the opinion of the רבנן
A steward or manager appointed to handle someone's affairs

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
phrases.english: It enters our mind that when Rabbi Yoshiya said [his ruling]

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי לָא מָצֵי מֵיפֵר,
phrases.english: [he said it] according to the Rabbis, who say he cannot cancel,
phrases.notes: He means the husband can't cancel vows before they're made. That is the source quoted in step 5.

phrases.english: and if not for the fact that the Merciful One said
"Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it,"
the steward would be able to cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the inference of step 4 with the source of step 5 to complete the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle from step 2, given in defense of רבא, that a person only appoints a שליח for something he himself could do right now.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן, the husband cannot cancel future vows, yet only the פסוק stops the steward. So a שליח could, in principle, do what the sender cannot do now.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יאשיה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. Maybe רבי יאשיה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that a husband can cancel vows ahead of time. If so, the steward is only doing what the husband himself could do.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe רבי יאשיה follows רבי אליעזר, who says the husband can cancel vows ahead of time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge by suggesting that רבי יאשיה holds like a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if רבי יאשיה follows the רבנן. If he follows רבי אליעזר, the husband can cancel future vows himself. Then the steward is not doing anything beyond the husband's power, and רבא's rule stands.

phrases.english: But perhaps [Rabbi Yoshiya holds] according to Rabbi Eliezer,
who says he can cancel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption in step 6 that רבי יאשיה follows the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא against רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed רבי יאשיה follows the רבנן. He may instead follow רבי אליעזר, for whom the husband can cancel future vows himself.

steps.title: Then why appoint a steward at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the pushback. If the husband can cancel future vows himself, why bother appointing a steward? He should simply cancel them before he leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does he need to appoint an agent? Let him cancel her vows himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the רבי אליעזר suggestion from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband has the power to cancel ahead of time, appointing a steward seems pointless. This makes it look unlikely that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, לְמָה לִי לְשַׁוּוֹיֵי שָׁלִיחַ?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need to appoint an agent?
Let him cancel [the vows] for her himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְמָה לִי לְשַׁוּוֹיֵי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband can cancel ahead of time, appointing a steward would be pointless.

steps.title: He worries he might forget, get angry or be busy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the husband appoints a steward because he worries that before his trip he might forget, be angry, or be too busy to cancel the vows himself. So the ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר, and there is no proof against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thinks: maybe I will forget, or I will be angry, or I will be too busy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why someone who could cancel vows himself would still appoint a steward. This saves רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Appointing the steward is a practical backup, not a sign that the husband lacks the power. So the ברייתא can fit רבי אליעזר, and the principle from step 2 (that a שליח only does what the sender could do now) still stands, along with רבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be busy or distracted

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the steward does not disprove רבא. It can follow רבי אליעזר, and the steward is appointed only as a practical backup.

phrases.english: He thinks: perhaps I will forget,
or I will be angry, or I will be busy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and closes the challenge to רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical explanation that removes the difficulty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Appointing a steward only makes sense if the husband cannot cancel the vows himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even someone who can cancel may appoint a steward as a backup against forgetting, anger or busyness, so רבא's rule stands.

steps.title: משנה: two people each vow to pay for half a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: someone vows to pay for 'shaving half a נזיר,' and his friend vows the same. רבי מאיר says each must pay for a whole נזיר's offerings. The חכמים say each pays half.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I take upon myself to shave half a נזיר,' and his friend hears and says 'And I take upon myself to shave half a נזיר,' each one pays for a whole נזיר, according to רבי מאיר. The חכמים say each one pays for half a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about a vow to cover half the cost of a נזיר's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Shaving a נזיר' means paying for the offerings a נזיר brings when he finishes and shaves. רבי מאיר makes each person pay in full, while the חכמים let each pay half, so together they cover one נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (introduces the text of the משנה)
To pay for half of a נזיר's shaving offerings
A whole נזיר (full set of offerings)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: "It is upon me to shave half a nazirite,"
phrases.notes: To 'shave' a נזיר means paying for the offerings he brings when he shaves at the end of his נזירות.

phrases.english: and his friend heard and said
"And I, it is upon me to shave half a nazirite"
this one shaves a whole nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה מְגַלֵּחַ נָזִיר שָׁלֵם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and that one shaves a whole nazirite. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
this one shaves half a nazirite,
and that one shaves half a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The earlier sugya is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: each vower pays for a whole נזיר. חכמים: each pays for half.

steps.title: רבא: what everyone agrees on, and why
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides agree on two cases. If someone says 'half the offerings of a נזיר,' he brings half. If he says 'the offerings of half a נזיר,' he must bring all of them, because there is no such thing as half a נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that if a person says 'half the offerings of a נזיר are upon me,' he brings half an offering. If he says 'the offerings of half a נזיר are upon me,' he must bring the whole offering. Why? Because we never find נזירות in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא marks out two cases where רבי מאיר and the חכמים do not disagree, and he gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words matters. 'Half of the offerings' divides the offerings, so he owes half. 'Offerings of half a נזיר' speaks about half a person's נזירות, which cannot exist, so it becomes a whole נזיר and he owes everything. This narrows the משנה's argument to the vague wording 'shave half a נזיר.'
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word order: 'half of the offerings of a נזיר' means half, but 'the offerings of half a נזיר' means the full amount.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exact wording of a vow decides what a person owes, and it sets up the question of where the משנה's argument really lies.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said: Everyone agrees
that wherever one said
"Half the offerings of a nazirite are upon me"
he brings half the offering.
[If he said] "The offerings of half a nazirite are upon me"
he needs to bring the whole offering.
What is the reason?
Because we have not found nazirite status in halves.
phrases.notes: If you accept half a נזירות, you are a full נזיר, so 'half a נזיר' really means a whole one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute of the משנה in step 10 by pointing out cases everyone agrees on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Half the offerings of a נזיר' means half. 'The offerings of half a נזיר' means all of them, since there is no half נזירות.

steps.title: רבא explains where and why רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the dispute is only about the משנה's exact wording. רבי מאיר holds that 'הרי עלי' already obligates the full offerings. The חכמים hold that the vow carries its own opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue when the person used the משנה's wording. רבי מאיר says that once he said 'it is upon me,' he owes all the נזיר offerings, and adding 'half a נזירות' cannot take that back. The חכמים say this is a vow that comes with its own way out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues from step 11. He now pinpoints the one case where the two sides really argue, and he explains each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, both sides agreed on the two clear wordings. Now רבא says the argument is only over 'the shaving of half a נזיר,' which could be read either way. רבי מאיר follows the first words, 'הרי עלי,' which created a full obligation. The חכמים read the whole sentence together, so his own words limit the vow to half.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me': the words that create an obligation to bring an offering
It is not in his power (to undo what he already took on)
A vow that has its 'opening' (way out) built right into it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on clear wordings. The argument is only over 'shaving half a נזיר.' רבי מאיר says the first words create a full obligation, and the חכמים say the whole sentence limits the vow.

phrases.english: And when they disagree,
they disagree about the wording of the משנה.
phrases.notes: He means the exact words from step 10: 'I take upon myself the shaving of half a נזיר.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
once he said "it is upon me,"
he became obligated in all of the nazirite offerings,
and when he then says "half a naziriteship,"
it is not in his power to take it back.
And the Rabbis hold:
it is a vow with its opening along with it.
phrases.notes: An 'opening' is a way out of a vow. Here his own word 'half' shows he never meant to take on the full offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement from step 11. After the agreed cases, he identifies the disputed case and the reason behind each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only over 'shaving half a נזיר.' רבי מאיר says the full obligation begins at 'הרי עלי' and cannot be cut down. The חכמים say the vow's own words limit it to half.

steps.title: New משנה: a vow to be a נזיר when a son is born
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vows to be a נזיר 'when I have a son' becomes a נזיר only if a son is born. A daughter, טומטום, or אנדרוגינוס does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I am a נזיר when I have a son,' and a son is born, he is a נזיר. If a daughter, a טומטום, or an אנדרוגינוס is born, he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a נזירות vow that only takes effect if something happens. Here the condition is having a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow depends exactly on the word 'son.' A daughter is clearly not a son. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not definitely male, so the condition has not clearly been met, and the vow does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the start of a new משנה
'I am a נזיר when I have a son': a vow that depends on a future event
A baby whose gender cannot be identified
A baby with both male and female features

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"I am hereby a nazirite when I will have a son,"
and a son was born to him,
he is a nazirite.
If a daughter, a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite was born to him,
he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: a נזירות vow that depends on a future birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow tied to 'a son' takes effect only when a definite son is born.

steps.title: The משנה continues: a vow to be a נזיר when a child is born
steps.stepSummary: If the person said 'when I have a child,' any baby counts, even a daughter, טומטום, or אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'when I have a child,' then even if a daughter, a טומטום, or an אנדרוגינוס is born, he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the contrasting case. A wider word, 'child,' makes any birth count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from the previous step is one word: 'child' instead of 'son.' 'Child' covers every baby, so the condition is met no matter what kind of baby is born.
steps.whatToRemember: The exact word chosen decides the vow. 'Son' means only a definite boy, while 'child' means any baby.

phrases.english: If he said "when I will have a child,"

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ נוֹלַד לוֹ בַּת, טוּמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
phrases.english: even if a daughter, a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite was born to him,
he is a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to step 13 by changing 'son' to 'child.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow tied to 'a child' takes effect with the birth of any baby.
